newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees slower growth in oils/fats output.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees slower growth in oils/fats output.

text.p: Global output of oils and fats in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) season is forecast at 97.71 million tonnes, up from 96.35 million in 95/96, but below 97.81 million forecast last December, the Oil World newsletter said.
Seed oil output should fall because oilseeds supplies are down and crushings have been curbed. This should only be partly offset by area-driven gains in palm oil production.
World consumption of oils and fats in 96/97 was forecast at 98.95 million tonnes compared with 95.85 million in 95/96.
Most consumption gains were seen in palm oil, sun oil, groundnut oil and olive oil and most declines in rape oil, cotton, sesame and linseed oil.
High oils and fats carry-in stocks last October had so far masked the tight scenario which would unfold more clearly in the period up to September, Oil World said.
Stocks in China, the former USSR, western Europe, Brazil, Malaysia and Turkey were falling fast.
Consumption in China, India, Indonesia, the European Union, the United States and Brazil was expanding.
Oil World saw exporters in the U.S., Argentina, Brazil and Malaysia benefiting from the rising demand.
